what: Duration regex uses (\S.*) for nodeid but requires verbatim preservation
scenario_or_breakage: Real CI --durations=0 lines include parametrized nodeids with spaces (e.g. test_retry.py::test_parity_is_transient_net_signature[fatal: unable to access ...]); \S.* truncates at the first space so assignments never match item.nodeid and rebalance data is wrong
suggested_fix: In plan.txt ### NEW: python/pytest_ci_timing.py, change the duration capture to (.+)$ (strip only trailing whitespace) after the setup|call|teardown phase; add a test_pytest_ci_timing.py fixture using the test_retry.py nodeid shape

what: Job filter is startswith('python-tests') which also matches python-tests-gate
scenario_or_breakage: .github/workflows/ci.yaml:644-645 names the aggregate job python-tests-gate; combined gh logs can include its lines under a job column that still satisfies startswith, diverging from the harness model (gh.py:947 anchors test-harnesses (\d+)) and risking stray parses if gate output ever resembles a duration row
suggested_fix: In plan.txt ### NEW: python/pytest_ci_timing.py, restrict to matrix jobs only (e.g. re.match(r'^python-tests \(', job_name) or equivalent); extend test_pytest_ci_timing.py to assert python-tests-gate lines are ignored

what: Job-name shard fallback is underspecified for python-version tuples
scenario_or_breakage: Fallback text says final integer inside (python-tests (3.11, 1) -> 1) but a naive first-\d+ match inside parentheses can yield 3 from 3.11, mis-assigning every row to the wrong shard and breaking observed_shard_count / --n-python-shards gating
suggested_fix: Pin the fallback in plan.txt (e.g. last integer token inside the parenthesized suffix, or re.search(r',\s*(\d+)\)\s*$', job_name)); add a test_pytest_ci_timing.py case for python-tests (3.11, 2) when step text lacks shard N of M
